commit.message:
fix(doctor): preserve offline migrations through service policy drift (#175492)

On a stopped systemd-managed npm-global Gateway (2026.6.11 -> 2026.9.33), doctor --fix ended 'Doctor could not complete maintenance' and never applied the required state-DB migration, so the Gateway could not start. prepareSystemdGatewayMaintenance returned false both for 'nothing to change' and for failure, and a stale system-owned definition observation kept refusing after the system unit was removed. Maintenance now returns unchanged / refreshed / failed, ignores stale capability observations, checks live ownership before backup and publication, and treats live system ownership as an advisory refusal without unnecessary rollback recovery.

Fixes #175400

commit.message:
ci: balance PostgreSQL conformance shards

Route database-engine *.integration.test.ts files to the integration
shard instead of assigning the entire directory to infra. Discover files
recursively so future command integration suites inherit the same owner
rule. Keep both jobs, their worker policies, and the 30-minute timeout.
Add --list for database-free inspection of the selected targets.

Main runs 39025102777 and 39028849280 measured infra/integrations at
27.58/10.57 and 29.07/10.08 minutes. Replaying their observed per-file
spans with the existing three-worker budget projects 18.51/19.78 and
19.01/19.16 minutes, retaining measured preparation and other projects.
Combined job-minutes remain approximately flat (38.15 -> 38.29 and
39.15 -> 38.17); the critical path gains 8-10 minutes and retains over
10 minutes of timeout margin. Natural CI will measure the actual result.

Validation: conformance runner tests 4/4 with --maxWorkers=1; targeted
test types, script/test typed lint, syntax and formatting checks pass.
Dry-run inventory partitions all 84 targets without overlap or loss.
P0-P2 review found no actionable issues.

external production caller to prepareUnwrittenWebhookCompletion and the
awaited async machine-state writer. Keep the synchronous recorder private
for its existing update-rehearsal caller; do not remove completion writes.

managed-symlink test. Use the same database for rehearsal and later boot,
and retain the fresh-profile and byte-preservation assertions.

typed/boundary lint and formatting. Deadcode scans no longer report this
export; unrelated diagnostic and test-support findings remain.

commit.message:
perf(channels): claim idle ingress during durable admission (#175459)

Append and claim eligible idle singleton messages through the existing ingress worker and drain. Preserve retry ordering, deduplication, claimant ownership, durable acknowledgment, and restart recovery. Reuse Telegram admission facts instead of inspecting the same fresh event again.

Focused owner and transport tests, live Telegram singleton proof, types, lint, source contracts, and database ratchets validate the change. Inherited CI findings, SDK comparison limits, and the queue-decorator follow-up are documented in the PR.

commit.message:
fix: batch PostgreSQL transcript search rows with repeated IDs (#175431)

Allocate transcript FTS identities by entry position and ordered sequence IDs, preserving recent-search and cold-export chronology while removing repeated-message-key batch splitting.

Native PostgreSQL conformance covers nullable/repeated IDs, exact row mapping, pooled-connection chronology, and SQLite-equivalent search cutoffs. A 67-row retained batch uses 2 statements instead of 34. Both PostgreSQL CI shards pass; three alternating Gateway pairs show unchanged warmed causal counts of 61 SQL / 16 requests / 0 MAIN.

retain their options and module graphs after their callers disappear.

SQLite custody and retire the plugin observation cache with its bus.

and Node. Release-note context: reduce retained worker and Gateway test
module graphs without weakening native worker cleanup.

commit.message:
test(worker): diagnose abort gate failures

The hourly lifecycle-fence failure reports only the child's cancellation
error, hiding which earlier gate was lost. Preserve the original cause and
record the boundary, elapsed cancellation time, reached gates, and transcript
request count, without emitting message content.

This does not claim a cancellation-runtime fix. Main d93ad5fc0e31 passes all
eight cases before this change (78.01s Vitest), and the diagnostic candidate
passes all eight (44.71s Vitest, 85.56s wrapper). The abort RPC success was
already asserted in the hourly failure; early child exit remains unclassified.
The fixed cancellation grace and submitted transcript failure are distinct
possibilities that the original log cannot separate.

Other-core test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and isolated P2
review pass. Only mechanical formatting follows review. Every assertion,
deadline, and cancellation/authority check remains unchanged. No hourly or
PR workflow dispatch or rerun.

test(sessions): close the incognito compaction fixture owner

The incognito accounting case added by #175311 retained its memory owner
past the file's lifetime. In the compact runtime-config shard, the next
placement-evidence suite therefore saw a second unrelated owner even though
all identity results were correct. Close the exact case-owned database at
test completion, including failure, without changing the shared directory
helper or any production path.

Reproduced on main d93ad5fc0e31: compaction then placement gave 10 passing
cases and the same owner-list failure. The repaired pair passes 11/11 in
both cached order and the original compaction-first order (43.94s wrapper,
37.10s Vitest). Agents-sessions test types, targeted type-aware lint,
formatting and isolated P2 autoreview pass. Assertions and deadlines are
unchanged. No CI reruns or dispatches.

commit.message:
test(process): restore runtime after broken broker fixture

The loader fixture added by ec23eefc9662 (#175206) can receive bootstrap
EPIPE before native exit. Closing then records its intentional loader
failure as a shutdown error. Awaiting that close before restoring
process.execPath leaked the synthetic Node path into later process tests;
removing the fixture left those tests spawning a nonexistent executable.

Restore the original runtime before cleanup. Validate only the exact
expected loader shutdown error, and prove a fresh broker starts afterward.
Keep every readiness, stderr, descriptor, and lifecycle assertion. The
runtime detector correctly diagnosed the broken fixture; production code
is unchanged.

Reproduced the original failure on Linux with host-stderr.test.ts under
--maxWorkers=1 --repeats 30 (1 failed, 4 passed; 29.17s wrapper).
After repair, seven selected files pass 40 tests on Linux (12.09s), and
six process files pass with --maxWorkers=4 --repeats 10 (26.90s), including
both real EMFILE cases. On macOS the same serial proof passes 38 tests
with two Linux-only skips (46.22s wall), and parallel pressure passes
27 tests with those same skips (96.99s wall).

Targeted services test types, normal/boundary lint, formatting and P2
review pass. No retries, timeout changes, or production recovery changes.

commit.message:
fix(doctor): scope btrfs NOCOW repair to SQLite files (#175474)

On btrfs, the Doctor NOCOW repair rewrote the entire agent store directory (thousands of unrelated files such as codex-home/, GBs) and spawned getfacl/setfacl per entry with no progress output, so doctor --fix looked hung for ~18 minutes and interrupted runs restarted from zero. The repair now exchanges only the SQLite family files (db/-wal/-shm/-journal) with hash-verified, synced copies and retained originals, batches ACL work, reports progress, and detects its own interrupted staging. Unrelated trees are untouched.

Fixes #175373

commit.message:
fix(test): stabilize catalog worker retention on Bun (#175486)

Measure catalog callback liveness through finalization notifications and collect from native immediate callbacks, outside JSC promise continuations. Preserve the strict one-callback retention bound and the collection control.
